value: A pointed set, also known as a based or rooted set, is a fundamental mathematical concept defined as an ordered pair comprising a set and a designated element within it, known as the base point. Maps between pointed sets, called based maps, are functions that preserve these specific base points. This structure constitutes a simple algebraic system, forming a category where based maps act as homomorphisms. Notably, this category is equivalent to the category of sets with partial functions, where the base point serves as a "default value" for undefined arguments. It is also a pointed category, featuring singleton sets as both initial and terminal (zero) objects. The concept of a distinguished point is pervasive, underpinning the definition of many algebraic structures, such as groups, where the identity element acts as the base point.
